newsitem.title: USA: Credit Store posts Q1 loss of $4.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Credit Store posts Q1 loss of $4.6 mln.

text.p: Credit Store Inc, a sub-prime lender, said Monday it posted a loss of $4.6 million or $0.15 a share for its first quarter ended March 31, 1997.

Revenues for the first quarter totaled $2.8 million, of which $1.8 million was derived from the company's portfolio of consumer receivables, $663,000 from various servicing contracts, and $327,000 from other sources.
Operating expenses in the quarter totaled $7 million.
Credit Store began its operations on October 8, 1996.

In another development, Credit Store said it agreed to acquire two portfolios of non-performing debt including $141.6 million in gross principal of automobile deficiency paper and $281 million in charged-off credit receivables from a money center bank.
After completion of these transactions, the gross principal on non-performing debt acquired the company will be about $1.87 billion.
Credit Store markets credit cards to consumers who had an interruption in the repayment of their debt and may be excluded from financing through traditional sources.
Shares of Credit Store rose 1-3/4 to 8-3/4.
